commits.author: forklady42
commits.message:
[taskforge] Repair tasks written by other sources (#12211)

Taskforge can now repair a task that another source wrote, such as a
SWE-rebench task converted to a TaskSpec outside Taskforge. The driver
accepts a `<name>.task.json` TaskSpec, with optional
`<name>.controls.json` controls, next to proposals; its `--proposals`
flag, and `run_taskforge.py`'s, is renamed `--inputs`. A source task has
no proposal and starts at validate. If its controls meet their expected
grades and its solve rate is in the band, review accepts it without an
author session. Otherwise review sends it to a new author session opened
from the `author.repair` prompt. Review asks for controls when the
source supplied none. The modify after a source task's first review is
not charged against `budget.max_modify_rounds`, because no author has
worked on the task yet; a source task gets as many author sessions as a
proposal.

The driver sets `sandbox.source_images` to the source task's own task
and grader images, and lowering refuses any other image for that task.
The author works in the task's environment when its image is a source
image. When that environment's setup fails, the author works in
`author.image` instead. When a setup command fails, RolloutEngine raises
`MachineSetupError`. Taskforge grades the affected solver trials and
controls as invalid tasks, which review returns to the author; before,
it retried them and held the workpiece. The driver also records the
source task's `id` and `source` in policy, and lowering refuses a
revision that changes either, so the author's `submit` reports it in the
same session. The driver refuses to resume a published run whose input
file has changed, or whose events have no workpiece, and leaves that
run's published result in place; checkpoints now publish the workpiece
before the events.

Taskforge does not build images. The TaskTrove SWE-rebench TaskSpecs
name Dockerfiles but no built images, and stage their repository at run
time through a `shell:v1` tool provider that Taskforge does not
implement, so they need a separate preparation step before this path can
run them. That step is a proposed follow-up. Other follow-ups: the
verifier reset clears the grader's working directory between grades,
which removes a repository the grader keeps there; the sandbox is fixed
at 1 CPU / 8 GiB; and the command timeout is 30 s. A source task
delivered without images has no admitted images, so lowering does not
check its task image, as it does not for a generated task. Code tells a
source task apart by `proposal is None` in about seven places; an origin
type could replace those checks if another kind of input appears. The
Taskforge unit tests pass locally with fakes. In a smoke run on Iris,
one known-good SWE-rebench V2.1 task ran from its upstream Docker Hub
image through validate, review and two author sessions to acceptance.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[levanter] Stream Hugging Face files straight into the model cache (#12206)

The model-cache prepare job downloaded each Hugging Face file to a local
scratch directory under `/tmp`, uploaded it, and then deleted it. That
fails for checkpoints with large files. Iris mounts `/tmp` as tmpfs on
Docker workers, which counts against the job's 8 GB memory limit, so
`google/gemma-4-31B-it` (a 49.8 GB shard) was OOM-killed on a GCP CPU
worker. On CoreWeave the job's 64 GB disk request is an
ephemeral-storage limit, and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (a
101.5 GB file) was killed with exit 137.

`_stream_hf_snapshot` now opens each file with `HfFileSystem` in
streaming mode and copies it into the cache filesystem through a 64 MB
buffer. No file touches local disk, and memory stays bounded regardless
of file size. Eight files copy concurrently, largest first. Resume
behavior is unchanged: files already in the cache at the expected size
are skipped, every upload is size-checked, and the completion marker is
written only after all files succeed.

| Copy path, same GCP CPU worker (4 CPU, 8 GB), 8 GLM-5.3-Flash shards |
42.9 GB took | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Download to scratch, then upload, one file at a time (before) | 573 s
| 75 MB/s |
| Stream 8 files concurrently (after) | 374 s | 115 MB/s |

A single stream runs at about 50 MB/s, so a repo dominated by one very
large file copies more slowly than one with many shards. DeepSeek's
101.5 GB file takes about 35 minutes, within the job's 4-hour timeout.
With an earlier single-stream version of this change, Gemma and DeepSeek
prepared successfully on the eval launcher. The tests in
`lib/levanter/tests/test_model_cache.py` and
`tests/inference/test_model_prepare.py` now fake `HfFileSystem` in place
of `hf_hub_download` and cover mirroring, resume, a truncated Hub
stream, private-token use, and the completion marker.

Part of #12156.

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Pin DS-1000's mini-200 verifier to the corrected revision (#12312)

The registry's DS-1000 packages derived the Harbor reward from
`run_test.py`'s exit code, and `run_test.py` runs the test program under
`except Exception`, which does not catch `SystemExit`: a solution
calling `sys.exit(0)` or `os._exit(0)` left the verifier with code 0 and
scored 1.0 without running an assertion (#12200). Task 701's
`exec_context` appended `.numpy()` to the inserted text, so the
assembled program was a `SyntaxError` and the task scored 0.0 for every
candidate, its own reference included.

Published
[penfever/harbor-datasets@cedf53d719](https://github.com/penfever/harbor-datasets/commit/cedf53d7193626b466c856b5021c4056106bfd84)
— a new revision on top of the pinned 791c0607, no history rewrite,
minimal diff (201 files):

- `test.sh` (the 200 mini-200 packages; the other 800 keep their older
verifier) now removes any stale reward, keeps `run_test.py`'s reward —
written only after the test program's assertions pass — counts a missing
file as 0, and still passes the exit code through for the verdict type.
- Task 701's `exec_context` inserts the solution as statements and
converts `result` after insertion, so a solution file with a trailing
newline assembles to valid Python; a bare expression still fails as
before.

Archive digest
`0f5f1022b497ebf9a70b7ab4803a1e77048cf2bca43081a1c9e08ede0ce29872`.

Verifier probes run against the pinned packages in the task environment:

| Probe | Pinned revision | This revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sys.exit(0)` | reward 1.0 | reward 0.0 |
| `os._exit(0)` | reward 1.0 | reward 0.0 |
| failed assertion | reward 0.0 | reward 0.0, exit 1 unchanged |
| passing probe | reward 1.0 | reward 1.0 |
| package 3 reference | reward 1.0 | reward 1.0 |
| task 701 reference | reward 0.0 (`SyntaxError`) | reward 1.0 |

The recipe and protocol version move to 2026.11.25, so the corpus
rebuilds and historical runs stay comparable: DS-1000 scores recorded
before this change are not comparable with runs after it.

Fixes #12200

commits.author: gonzalobenegas
commits.message:
[eval] Add SWE-bench Science to the curated catalog (#12109)

Add SWE-bench Science to the curated TaskSpec catalog using the dataset
release pinned at `997408298e8e4d09978b1120b95c4540d1a71bcb`. The Pi
protocol covers 118 of the 119 upstream tasks. The catalog excludes task
019 (pycisTopic) pending permission to modify the package. Release
tooling is MIT licensed and task materials retain their upstream
licenses.

The Hugging Face reader normally looks for `<task>/task.toml` at the
repository root. This release puts the manifests one level deeper, for
example `tasks/task_002/task.toml`. Setting `root="tasks"` lets Marin
reuse its package discovery and archiving code, following the same
convention it already uses for repositories downloaded as tarballs. The
directory enters the download cache key only when specified, so existing
sources keep their cached artifacts.

The pinned release uses Pier’s task manifest schema 1.3. Marin’s shared
Harbor importer accepts schemas 1.0 through 1.2 and expects collection
commands in `verifier.collect`. SWE-bench Science instead supplies a
`pre_artifacts.sh` script that exports the solver’s changes as
`model.patch`. The benchmark-local converter maps this directly to a
Marin `TaskSpec`. After Pi exits, Marin runs the script in the solver
workspace and copies the patch into a fresh, digest-pinned verifier that
runs the upstream grader. Each upstream verifier requests 2 CPUs, 8 GiB
of RAM, and 20 GiB of disk. The catalog preset grades with the evaluator
worker’s available resources and does not enforce those limits per
verifier.

Pi 0.87.0 runs in the solver image with xhigh reasoning, a 65,536-token
context and a 16,384-token reply cap.

All 118 catalog tasks matched the pinned release on instructions, image
digests and timeouts. Both Qwen3.8-27B reference runs graded this same
set. [Issue
#12108](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/12108) records
the scores, license decisions and same-patch verifier check.

Fixes #12108

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[docs] Run local SkyRL commands with uv --isolated --frozen (#12286)

Documented local SkyRL commands materialized a `vendor/skyrl/.venv` in
every
checkout; a recent macOS cleanup measured about 90 RL worktrees carrying
one.

The local commands in docs/dev-guide/skyrl.md and
docs/references/rl-launching.md now run as
`uv run --isolated --frozen --project vendor/skyrl ...`. `--isolated`
builds
the environment in the shared uv cache instead of a per-checkout
`.venv`, and
`--frozen` pins the install to the lockfile. Each command keeps its
extras and
arguments. The checkpoint-export rerun command also switched
`--directory` to
`--project`: with `--isolated` the environment comes from the project,
and the
module resolves its paths from the given arguments, like the neighboring
export command.

The docs now state that the `cpu` extra runs on macOS while the `vllm`
and
`megatron` extras and GPU torch builds do not; GPU jobs run on Iris.

`skyrl_cpu_command` in lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py keeps building
`uv run --project vendor/skyrl --frozen ...` without `--isolated`: the
same
argv also runs inside Iris task images (the CPU cat-count nightly),
which this
per-worktree cleanup does not target, and the launcher-environment test
pins
the project `.venv` behavior. Converting it stays a separate decision.

Measured on macOS with uv 0.13.5 in a fresh worktree: two runs of the
documented `marinskyrl --help` command took 25.9 s and 20.7 s, created
no
`vendor/skyrl/.venv`, and lowered free disk by about 52 MiB (`df`). The
shared
cache stores the wheels once; uv rebuilds the ephemeral isolated
environment
on each run in about 2 s warm, and a second fresh worktree linked its
own
editable paths with no `.venv`.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[evals] Add ChemBench as a curated evaluation (#11831)

Add [ChemBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jablonkagroup/ChemBench)
([Mirza et al., Nature Chemistry
2025](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41557-025-01815-x)) as the
`chembench` curated chat benchmark. It asks 2,785 chemistry questions
from nine topic files at revision `6e1d2574`: 2,542 multiple choice, 395
of them with several correct options, and 243 with a numeric answer.
Scores are fraction correct overall and per topic. Prompts, option
lettering, markup stripping and `[ANSWER]`-tag parsing follow the
authors' runner,
[lamalab-org/chembench](https://github.com/lamalab-org/chembench) at
`45f8bad0`. A multiple-choice answer must name exactly the correct
letters; a numeric answer must be within 1% of the target. Decoding is
greedy with thinking enabled, and only the final answer is graded. The
dataset and the runner are MIT-licensed. The benchmark is not added to a
suite.

The prompts match the authors' published per-question Llama reports byte
for byte on 2,710 of 2,785 rows; the other 75 rows were edited in the
dataset after that run. On those 2,710 responses our grader agrees with
the authors' grades on 99.2% (2,689). The 21 disagreements come from the
deliberate differences below, refusal-detector false positives in the
authors' runner, and one gold answer changed after their run. The
authors' runner differs in four ways. It sends untagged answers to an
LLM extractor; here they score zero. Its numeric tolerance uses `0.01 *
target`, which no answer meets for a zero or negative target; here it
uses the target's magnitude. Its pint unit parsing is replaced by
arithmetic for the number forms its regex accepts. Its number pattern
matches the literal text `\u00d7`; here it matches the × sign. No
reference model was run: the Llama 3.1 8B weights the authors report are
gated for the cluster's Hugging Face token.

| Model | Hardware | Scored | Accuracy ± SE | Hit 73,728-token limit |
Unparsed, not truncated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Muse Glimmer 30B | H100x2 | 2785/2785 | 0.671 ± 0.009 | 7 (0.3%) | 0 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super | H100x4 | 2785/2785 | 0.687 ± 0.009 | 103 (3.7%) |
9 |
| Snowball v0.1 | H100x8 | 2785/2785 | 0.633 ± 0.009 | 44 (1.6%) | 9 |

Truncated responses score zero. Nemotron's are mostly long reasoning (17
of 103 repeat); 62 are in `chemical_preference`. Snowball's truncations
are repetition loops (41 of 44). The audit read every unparsed response,
every wrong numeric answer and every multiple-choice response that was
not a bare tag, and found no wrong grade. 17 of the 18 unparsed
responses open `[ANSWER]` but never close it; the authors' regex also
rejects these. Accepting them would add six correct answers for Nemotron
and none for the other models. Two gold answers look wrong and are kept
as published: `materials_science` row 10 omits the aliquot step, so the
stated question gives 0.00194 rather than 0.0097, and the B2H6 enthalpy
question in `physical_chemistry` has garbled signs.

| Model | Hardware | Start to finish | Inference GPU-hours | $ (H100
list) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Muse Glimmer 30B | H100x2 | 1h03m | 2.0–2.1 | 12–13 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super | H100x4 | 5h58m | 20.7–23.9 | 127–147 |
| Snowball v0.1 | H100x8 | 1h23m | 4.9–11.1 | 30–68 |

Each inference worker was preempted at least once. Iris reports only the
last attempt's duration, so each range runs from that attempt to the
job's start-to-finish time. The runs used `uv run python -m
experiments.evaluation.cli launch --model <model> --evals chembench
--priority interactive`.

commits.author: chrismc91

[eval] Add TruthfulQA binary choice (v2) as truthfulqa-binary (#12242)

Add `truthfulqa-binary`, the TruthfulQA authors' January 2025
binary-choice version. It reads 790 questions from the sha256-pinned
`TruthfulQA.csv` at sylinrl/TruthfulQA `d71c1108` (Apache-2.0). Each
question offers its Best Answer and Best Incorrect Answer as A and B, in
an order fixed by the low bit of `sha256(question)`. The default
`likelihood` protocol compares the two letters' log-probabilities. The
`chat` protocol (`--evals truthfulqa-binary-chat`) grades the final
`Answer: A|B` line with verifyit's `McqSpec` in a grader machine.
Upstream ships no runner, so both prompts are Marin's own. The v1 MC2
`truthfulqa` benchmark is unchanged.

`multiple_choice_evaluation` now accepts a `UrlSource`. A few-shot pool
file still requires an `HfSource`. Compiled output of existing
benchmarks is unchanged, so nothing republishes.

Validation on Glimmer 30B and Snowball v0.1, run records, and cost are
in #12241.

Fixes #12241

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[eval] Add FACTS Parametric public split judged by gpt-oss-120b (#12146)

Add `facts-parametric`, the 1,052 public questions of FACTS Parametric
([arXiv:2512.10791](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10791) §4, [Kaggle
benchmark](https://www.kaggle.com/benchmarks/google/facts-parametric)),
to the curated catalog. It asks closed-book factoid questions whose
answers are on Wikipedia, many of them terse search-style queries such
as `yair yint aung birthday`. Rows come from Kaggle dataset
`kaggle/facts-parametric-public-examples` version 2, pinned by URL and
SHA-256; the 1,052-row private split stays with Kaggle. Each question is
sent bare as one user message with thinking on, a 16,384-token cap and
model-default sampling, and only the final answer is graded. The
evaluation is not added to a suite.

The judge prompt is the [starter
notebook's](https://www.kaggle.com/code/yulongt/facts-parametric-benchmark-starter-code)
(version 10), byte for byte as vendored in NVIDIA-NeMo/Gym#3588. It
grades each answer CORRECT, MISTAKE, UNKNOWN or NOT_ATTEMPTED. Marin
asks `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Together once per answer, where the paper
averages three Gemini 2.5 Pro grades. Grading runs in process through
Verifyit's labels rubric, which now takes the verdict from the last
match of `JudgeSpec.verdict_patterns` when they are set, as its pairwise
rubric already does. The judge explains its grade before the `Output:`
line and often names other labels there, so the verdict is the last
`Output:` line rather than the notebook's substring rule, which reads
"not a MISTAKE" as MISTAKE. A reply with no `Output:` line is a grading
failure, so the attempt is retried. UNKNOWN counts as attempted and
incorrect, as in the paper, so the classification summary's attempted
accuracy and F1 follow the paper's definitions. Scores are reported per
topic. The dataset, the notebook and NeMo Gym are Apache 2.0.

Full runs on 2026-11-21, every row scored, no judge failures:

| Model | Hardware | Accuracy | Not attempted | Attempted accuracy | F1
| Truncated |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Nemotron 3.5 Super | H100x4 | 21.6% ± 1.3 | 36.7% | 34.1% | 0.264 | 3
|
| Muse Glimmer 30B | H100x2 | 11.2% ± 1.0 | 13.6% | 13.0% | 0.120 | 1 |
| Snowball v0.1 (`grug` parser) | H100x8 | 5.1% ± 0.7 | 26.0% | 6.9% |
0.059 | 62 |

There is no matched reference score. The paper and leaderboard use three
Gemini 2.5 Pro grades and pool the private split; for scale, the paper
reports Gemini 2.5 Flash at 30.6% and GPT-5 mini at 16%. NeMo Gym
reports Kimi K3 at 65.7% on the public split with that judge. A Kimi K3
reference through OpenRouter was dropped after its pinned Moonshot
provider rate-limited 5 of 20 smoke rows even at concurrency 2; its 15
graded rows scored 9 correct. Snowball's truncations are reasoning loops
(`Maybe it's "Megan Clark".` repeated 148 times); all 62 return an empty
answer and score NOT_ATTEMPTED, and answering them at its attempted
accuracy would add about 0.4 points.

A blinded audit had Claude and Codex grade 121 answers sampled by
verdict across the three models with the same rubric. The reviewers
agreed with each other on 118, and the judge matched that label on 112
of them (95%). Three of the six misses are refusals that name no answer,
such as "I don't have information about Regina Belle having a brother",
graded MISTAKE instead of NOT_ATTEMPTED, so hedging is slightly
undercounted; the others are one lenient CORRECT, one strict MISTAKE
("Khaqan Abbasi" for "Muhammad Khaqan Abbasi") and the single UNKNOWN.
Each reviewer flagged one possible item defect (Harrisburg's founder,
Top Deck's invention year), and they did not agree on either.

Costs, all on `cw-rno2a`:

| Model | Hardware | Start to finish | Final attempt | Accelerator-hours
(approx.) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Muse Glimmer 30B | H100x2 | 5.5 h | 2.1 h | 5–6.5 |
| Nemotron 3.5 Super | H100x4 | 5.8 h | 2.2 h | 12–13 |
| Snowball v0.1 | H100x8 | 5.6 h | 2.2 h | 18–26 |

The judge used 4.8M input and 0.67M output tokens across the three runs,
about $1.10 on Together. Interactive-priority workers were preempted up
to five times per run. The full runs graded through a sandboxed scorer
with the same prompt, judge settings and `Output:` rule; a 20-row Muse
Glimmer 30B run on the in-process judge scored every row with no judge
failures, and its three verdicts that differ from the full run follow
changed answers, where Glimmer named a wrong answer instead of
declining.

commits.message:
[infra] Raise the EvalDash ingest runner to 16 GiB and 4 CPUs (#12291)

Raise the `marina-evaldash` Cloud Run ingest job from 1 CPU and 1 GiB to
4 CPUs and 16 GiB in `infra/marina/runtime.toml`. Cloud Run requires at
least 4 vCPU for a memory limit above 8 GiB.

The ingest is killed for exceeding memory while it reconciles
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals`, which holds 17,525 record
directories. Cloud Run executions exit with code -9 and log
`Out-of-memory event detected in container`. EvalDash
`/evaldash/api/status` shows the last successful probe of that prefix at
2026-11-17T18:52Z, while `gs://marin-eval-metadata/evals` probes
normally. After the 86,400-second revalidation interval, every record is
due for re-parse in one pass, which 1 GiB cannot hold. As a result, no
CoreWeave eval record has reached the EvalDash catalog since November
17.

The `marina` matrix in `ops-pulumi-rollout` deploys this stack from
`main`, so the next rollout after merge updates the job's resources. A
follow-up change will make the reconcile stream records or work
incrementally, so memory stays bounded as the prefix grows.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[shellbox] Report a Daytona sandbox removed while starting as unavailable (#12268)

Daytona sometimes deletes a sandbox it has accepted before the sandbox
starts; the SDK's start wait then raises `DaytonaNotFoundError`
("Sandbox with ID or name … not found"). Daytona machine creation now
raises `MachineUnavailable` for it, which evaluation workers already
retry as an infrastructure failure.

evaluation run. Grader machines are created after the agent has run, and
an unrecognized error at that point is treated as permanent and
propagates out of the worker. A 25-task SWE-bench-Science smoke on
Daytona ended this way after 49 minutes, with 15 attempts still in
flight.

commits.author: amd-pratmish
commits.message:
[levanter] Commit a spilling checkpoint one manifest wave at a time (#11628)

A lock-file save whose staged bytes do not fit in
`max_staged_host_bytes` commits one atomic OCDBT transaction per staging
wave. Lock-file commits are serialized across clients, so a single
transaction for the whole save starts no chunk write until every chunk
is staged. A save that fits the budget still commits each chunk as soon
as it is staged. A non-atomic transaction published the array metadata
and the chunks as two manifest versions, so each wave uses one atomic
transaction. A PyTree that is a single array has an empty OCDBT path and
stays at the database root on this path and on the per-chunk path. Each
wave commit uses the same directory refresh and commit-order lock as a
per-chunk commit.

Process 0 also writes unsharded host leaves, so one process can spill
while another fits. Both paths publish metadata once and then wait at
the same barrier, so the save finishes either way.

Measured on two NFS clients, CPU only, before this change was rebased
onto `main`. Ten saves of 128 MiB arrays: one transaction per save took
29.2 s, per-chunk commits took 16.9 s, and neither setting had a failed
save. At an 8 MiB budget, waves took 33.6 s and per-chunk commits took
40.2 s. Twenty saves of 32 arrays of 4 MiB, also at an 8 MiB budget,
took 54.9 s with waves and 67.6 s with per-chunk commits, again with no
failed saves. On local disk, a single-process 128 MiB save took 0.30 s
per chunk and 0.37 s as one transaction. Waves were 35–45% slower than
per-chunk commits there, which is why a save that fits the budget does
not use them.

These timings were not re-run after the rebase. The empty-path fix does
not change how a named array is grouped into a wave.

Stacks on #11620. The lock-file behavior is that pull request.

commits.message:
[verifyit] Restore grading for unit chains and ordinals (#12197)

References with compound unit chains, ordinal superscripts, or signed
and spaced unit powers now grade against their numeric value. Since
#11989, the reference parser rejected a `/\mathrm{s}` tail, read
`11^{\text{th}}` as a symbolic exponent, and rejected `\text{s}^{-1}`.

The parser recognizes complete terminal unit chains, accepts bare powers
after text groups with nonletter content, and removes ordinal suffixes
only from numbers at the start of a reference. This preserves grading
for unit strings such as `\text{m/s}^2` and option references such as
`\textbf{(C)}\ 11^{\text{th}}`. Text groups followed by additional math
retain the existing fail-closed path.

The focused math-answer suite passed 205 tests. The affected runner
passed 1,954 Harbor unit tests, 21 Harbor runtime tests, 67 Harbor
driver tests, and 933 Marin and VerifyIt tests before the 600-second
session limit stopped that lane with no reported failure.

Fixes #12191

[rl] Stream prepared task cache reads and writes (#12237)

shards as the dataset workers run. Export those shards to one compressed

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Generate source identity and reconcile historical IDs (#11903)

Main's RL source declarations predate the Atlas source model:
`SourceInfo`
took free-form ids and string origins, and stored records written under
historical ids no longer match the generated identity. This PR generates
each
source's id and title from its typed upstream keys and resolves
historical ids
through an alias table where records are read: selection recipes,
eval-lite
panels, `--corpus` joins and catalog publication canonicalize both
sides, so a
recipe keyed by historical ids selects renamed sources unmodified and a
renamed source's prior assessment stays attached when it is republished.
The
alias table and `canonical_source_id` live in
`finestore.rl.source_identity`
beside `source_identifier`, where the catalog loader can import the same
helper. Publication re-keys a prior row matched through the alias table
onto
its generated identity, and the Atlas load compares a selected
assessment's
source through the same aliases, so a renamed source keeps one row and
its
carried assessment. The alias table covers the complete join of main's
published declarations onto their generated identities, pinned by the
checked-in rename join in `lib/finestore/tests/source_id_renames.json`.

`SourceInfo` now requires every source to state its typed
`data_restriction`
tier explicitly; `PRIVATE_ALWAYS` is inherited by the declaration and
every
derived artifact, and a downgrade is refused. `SourceInfo` also carries
`current_release`, declared `intended_use` and `license_receipt`, with a
`require_license` gate that fails closed, so the ingestion PRs cannot
construct
source work without a receipt.

The 32 pipeline-less Atlas-admitted records moved out of this PR per
review:
each lands with the import that makes it runnable, and the records as
approved
are preserved on
[`benfeuer/atlas-admitted-records`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/benfeuer/atlas-admitted-records).

Out of scope: the pinned-variant registry (no admitted source is a
registered
variant), the license-binding pipeline and its index data, and the
Atlas's
difficulty, QA, lexical and consumer machinery.

#11659 (versioned RL curriculum) follows this change; its entries select
pinned source records by generated id.

commits.author: chrismc91
commits.message:
[eval] Commit evaluation selections and attempt records in shared transactions (#12246)

Curated evaluation runs kept their inference servers almost idle. The
driver's single producer committed each selected case's selection row in
its own FineStore transaction and waited for it before dispatching the
case, and every started row and terminal result was another transaction
on the same writer thread. Each transaction writes shards, a manifest
and a conditional HEAD to object storage, so cases reached the consumers
about one commit at a time, roughly once a second against
`marin-us-east-02a`. Full TriviaQA runs scored 9 to 11 items per minute
on H100 servers that showed no running requests in most samples.

The producer now commits the selection rows of up to `concurrency` cases
together, then dispatches them; selections stay durable before their
cases run, and a resumed run rewrites its earlier selections in the same
batches. `_EvaluationWriter` commits all writes queued while its thread
was busy as one transaction. Each caller still returns only once its own
write is durable, so started rows precede model calls and an attempt's
terminal rows and evidence land together. Each write submits its own
drain to the executor, so every queued write commits before the store
closes, including a write whose caller was cancelled. A failed batch is
retried in halves, so only the failing write's caller sees its error. A
batch of one uses the unbounded transaction that oversized agent
evidence needs (#12243).

A regrade of 200 stored Glimmer 30B TriviaQA answers on an Iris CPU
worker, reusing every response so the model is never called, at
concurrency 64:

| | Commits, including compactions | First to last commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | 721 | 10 min 14 s |
| this branch | 63 | 2 min 05 s |

With the writer out of the way, about 64 Shellbox graders run at once on
the worker's 8 CPUs. Median grader setup rose from 0.4 s to 8.0 s and
grading from 0.8 s to 13.9 s, so the grading worker's CPU now bounds
throughput.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Release applets from a landed integration-branch checkout (#12164)

The `marina release` guard demands a clean checkout at origin's current
`main`, but the Atlas applet releases are cut from integration branches
such as `atlas-env-audit`, so no Atlas release has ever passed the guard
without `--allow-dirty` — the flag that releases branch or uncommitted
source *without* verified Git provenance. r39 shipped with it.

`marina release` gains `--release-branch <name>`: the guarded path
verifies a clean checkout whose HEAD origin's declared branch contains —
the branch tip or any commit already merged into it, checked against the
remote directly so a stale tracking ref or a CI rerun checkout still
refuses. Integration branches move ahead of the release cut while CI and
receipts run, so ancestry rather than equality is the landed contract
for a declared branch; default releases keep the exact origin-`main`
behavior unchanged. The release provenance records the branch it was cut
from, and `--allow-dirty` cannot combine with `--release-branch` — a
landed-checkout release never needs it.

Tests cover the tip and ancestor acceptance, the unlanded and dirty
refusals, the main-path equality semantics (including the detached CI
checkout and old-CI-rerun cases), the CLI-level provenance record and
pre-publish unlanded refusal, and the option-combination usage error.
